questions.stem: A shape is formed by a $12\text{ cm} \times 8\text{ cm}$ rectangle with a $4\text{ cm} \times 3\text{ cm}$ rectangle removed from one corner. What is the area of the remaining shape?
questions.explanation: Large rectangle area $= 12 \times 8 = 96\text{ cm}^2$. Removed rectangle $= 4 \times 3 = 12\text{ cm}^2$. Remaining area $= 96 - 12 = 84\text{ cm}^2$.

questions.stem: A T-shape is formed from two rectangles: a horizontal bar $14\text{ cm} \times 3\text{ cm}$ on top, and a vertical bar $4\text{ cm} \times 8\text{ cm}$ below. What is the total area?
questions.explanation: Horizontal bar area $= 14 \times 3 = 42\text{ cm}^2$. Vertical bar area $= 4 \times 8 = 32\text{ cm}^2$. Total $= 42 + 32 = 74\text{ cm}^2$.

questions.stem: When finding the area of a compound shape by subtraction, you should:

options.text: Calculate the area of the enclosing shape and subtract the missing parts
Multiply the perimeter by the height

questions.explanation: The subtraction method involves calculating the area of the full enclosing shape (e.g. a rectangle) and then subtracting the areas of any parts that have been removed.
